gravity_concepts:
-Gravity
Concepts
 1. Everything that has mass, pulls things around it towards itself. This pull,
 this force is called Gravity.
 2. Every particle, every object, every being, every celestial body, everything
 has mass, even if it is a teeny tiny bit of it - and they all exhibit Gravity -
 they all pull everything around them. I’m pulling you, you are pulling me,
 the Earth is pulling all of us, you are pulling the moon, the moon is pulling
 you. You are pulling all the tiny particles around you, you are pulling the
 Earth, The Earth is pulling you and all the particles around you. Gravity is
 everywhere. (F-G*m1*m2/r2)
 3. Imagine, you were just floating in space and there are no planets or stars or
 anything large around you for billions of miles. You would just be floating
 in space, in the same direction & speed you started with forever. (You can
 move your arms, legs, head, turn your body, but you can’t change your
 direction or speed. Can’t you swim? Not really because, for that you need
 enough particles with enough mass around you to push you back when you
 push them as you move your hand. ) Now imagine Earth appears say a 100
 miles from you, you would swiftly be pulled towards it, because it is so huge
 compared to you & can pull you easily, which it does naturally. But the
 moment Earth appears near where you are floating, not only does the Earth
 pull you, you starting pulling it too. But you wont end up moving the Earth
 because , as a comparatively smaller object, your gravity is not enough to
 pull a larger body. Similarly the Sun is pulling the Earth, other planets,
 other celestial bodies around itself. (are you pulling all the tiny particles
 around you? Are they all getting stuck to you ? or are they all circling
 around you, like Earth is around the Sun? Or are they all falling to the
 ground? What do you think is happening & why?)
 4. But, we said everything ,pulls. Does photon also have gravity? It has no
 mass. Its the only “particle” we know for sure has 0 mass at rest. - It does
 have gravity. Because turns out, it is not mass directly that causes gravity,
 but it is actually Energy. A photon that is travelling at speed C from the
 sun, has energy owing to its motion. This energy causes gravity. Earth also
 has Energy - Its energy is more in the “frozen” form so to speak, which
 manifests as mass. We see the mass first and think, that is causing the
 Energy (E=mc2) - but thats just how we measure Energy. It is infact energy
 that causes Mass. Mass is one form of Energy.
5. How does gravity arise? - Hold a blanket from 4 sides, drop a ball on it - it
 curves & stretches? - All particles, objects, beings, planets, and the Universe
 can be imagined to be suspended on a blanket like this - The Space-Time
 Blanket. Just as the ball, with some mass causes the blanket to curve, so
 does every particle, object, etc. (imagine the space, in which I am, you are,
 earth is, stars are, everything is - as a blanket stretched across time - there
 was space billions of years ago, there will be space billions of years from
 now, as long as Universe exists, it can only exist on space, for a time or
 maybe even forever, we dont know, unless we believe Universe began with
 Big Bang, so if there was a start, maybe there would be an end too; then
 another start , another end and so on.)
6. So an object as big as Earth, curves this Space Time blanket. On your
 blanket, drop a smaller ball near where you have placed the bigger ball.
 What happens? Does the ball roll along the curvature caused by the bigger
 ball, towards the center of the curvature? This curvature caused by the
 mass of an object is what causes this “pull” towards itself. Same applies for
 the massless photons too - their speed/energy/momentum interacts with
 space time bending it , causing Gravity.
 So I’m not really pulling you. There is no direct effort or energy. Earth is
 not pulling everything around it, Sun is not pulling the Earth. We each
  exist, we are here and that causes the curvature as a result, and the
 curvature in turn causes other objects to fall towards it. So the Gravity, we
 call a force, doesn’t need energy at all. Try pulling your friend, are you
 spending energy? Do you feel tired after a while? Is it work? - The
 gravitational pull is unlike this full pull. Cos the planet or the object is not
 doing any work or expending its energy. Energy (sometimes as mass)
 automatically alters the curvature. We fall along the curvature. The Energy
 of the object does not decrease because of this. (it could end up increasing
 because, once we fall into the center and burn, that energy is added on to
 that we fell into. )
7. Lets go back to you floating in space, Earth is now there all of a sudden, so
 space time fabric is curved, and you are naturally standing sliding into the
 curve to its center, which will be at the geometric center of our spherical
 earth. (we will see more about this later) . For now, you move along the
 curvature towards the center of the mass . But you land on the surface of
 the Earth , i.e. the ground. With this ends your flow along the Space time
 curve created by the Earth, because you can pass through the ground, you
 cannot reach the center of the mass/center of the ST curve. So Gravity , the
 space time curve is leading you to its center which is stopped by the ground
 and the opposing force, a push force that it exerts on you. You are able to
 stand on the ground, not because Gravity is pulling you towards itself,
 because if it can succeed, you would probably be dragged through a hole you
 will pierce as you move down the ground to the center of the earth, but
 because, the ground is pushing you and holding you. What is this push force
 you experience ?- the normal force - everything has a push force too - which
 acts when you apply a force against it , it pushes you - only upon contact,
 when my atoms and the objects atoms come close to each other and start
 repelling. Unlike gravity which is omnipresent. On solid ground the push
 force, is equal to the pull force of earth’s gravity. So you stand and dont get
  burrowed. On water, you float if the push force is equal to the force of
 gravity pulling towards the center - you sink, if the push force of the water
 is less. That's why you cannot float when the volume of water is not enough
 for your weight or when in an ocean you dont align your body in a way
 that compensates for the push force. If you are falling into air, its push force
 is much lesser than the earth's gravitational force & we would fall through.
 This Normal force that objects, particles, materials, exhibit depends on the
 density of the material - how densely the atoms are packed - more densely
 packed, they repel the force we apply better and are more solid. It is the
 Normal force = Fg =mg that the ground applies on me when I'm standing.
 It is the normal force = F i apply with my finger on a door , that i
 experience & keeps my digging into the door. Normal force is always equal
 and opposite to the force exerted upon itself. Fn while running on ground is
 usually 2-3* mg
8. Now, lets say, Jupiter appears, instead of the Earth. It is also huge compared
 to you & has a great energy and mass. You will as usual get dragged along
 the space time curvature it creates, which is also at its center. But with
 Jupiter you wont land anywhere. Jupiter is a Gas giant. It has no surface,
 no solid ground. Just gas, which gets thicker and thicker & hotter & hotter
 as you go down its center. So you will at some point be obliterated as you
 would if you were to fall through earth’s ground into its center too. Same
 case with the other gas giant , Saturn. But they look solid on photos? Its just
 the atmosphere and gas clouds we are seeing. Nothing but more gas below it.
 Neptune & Uranus on the other hand are ice giants - made of h20,ch4 &
 nh3(ammonia) - so its like a liquid swirling sphere colder on top, gets hotter
 towards the core. You would again not land, but sink, until the pressure &
 heat devours you.
9. Now say a black hole appears- you would again fall into it, since its
 extremely high Energy & mass are confined into what we imagine as a
  point, there is no landing, you would just fall towards the center and as
 usual be ripped off.
10.But, if we imagine a blanket and a ball on it, the center of the space time
 curvature is at the bottom of the ball, where it is touching the blanket. But
 we are saying the center of curvature with fall at the geometric center of the
 object. How? - Because space is not like a blanket, its not flat, 2dimensional
 - space is all around you, as you can see,and experience , in all directions &
 all dimensions. So when a space time curves because of Energy/Mass, it is
 not just in one direction, like how a blanket forms a curve only in one
 direction , but the space time curves radially in all directions around the
 object , thereby the center of curvature coinciding with the center of the
 object. This is not easy or even really possible to imagine these curvature,
 like how we can imagine a blanket curve. So we use that as an analogy to
 understand the behaviour. It does not exactly represent how ST behaves.
11. Now if gravity pulls all objects around its center, then what happens with
 photons, that have no mass & are in motion?
12.When we are floating in water we don’t really feel our weights, we feel
 almost weightless, when standing in water we feel like we weigh lesser than
 on ground, when floating in space, we feel nearly 0 weight - all because of
 the Normal Force of the ground or the water or the air - Gravity remains
 the same on ground or in a pool. Gravity of the earth is pulling you down
 with the same force - but the opposing normal force exerted by the ground is
 equal and opposite to mg, which is weight on ground is mg. But in water, its
 opposing normal force is lesser so our weight we feel is equal to that
 opposing force, and hence feel lighter. In air or space, we feel almost no
 Normal force because there is no dense object we are pressing against - even
 though gravity continues to act wherever we go . Although as we go away
 from the earth, the earth’s gravitational pull on us reduces, but we would
 also get into the gravitational fields of other celestial objects - all these
  gravity is constantly acting upon us, that we dont feel, cos we perceive
 gravity only through a normal force. We might experience 0 gravity, if we
 are able to reach deep space with no large bodies for millions of miles
 around us. Just because we feel weightless in space or while floating in an
 ocean, doesnt mean we are experiencing 0 gravity - it just means we are
 experiencing near weightlessness. Even inside the ISS - people float, not
 because they arent experiencing the earths gravity - they are, the ISS is -
 the ISS and everything inside is being pulled by the g (90% of whats on
 ground), but it is maintaining a velocity & sideways thereby revolving
 aru=ound the earth (15-16 orbits per day at 7.66km/S velocity) to keep it
 from falling into earth . The people and objects inside ISS are floating
 because, normal force is 0, not because gravity is 0.
13.ISS is surfing gravity waves - maintain a (orbital) velocity in sideways
 direction to the gravity - voila - surfing - while surfing too, the water’s slope
 pulls you down, you maintain a velocity and move sideways you can stay
 on the slope.
14.We saw how gravity bends space time , cos of which objects fall towards the
 center - how does it affect time? Time is slower closer to the center of
 gravitational field - Time Dialation Story
15.Is Gravity a quantum force - like the electromagnetic force, or atomic force,
 nuclear force ? - dont know yet -Gravitons ?
16.Universe - dance between the expanding force of dark energy and the
 attractive force of gravity - galaxies hold up, stars and plants stay clustered
 together within an expanding universe due to gravity
17.Gravitational lensing - light -photons -like any other particle or object also
 travels along the space time curvatures - leading to the them changing
 directions instead of their usual straight line -
18.Gravity weakens inside its surface and becomes 0 at the center - gravity is
 strongest at the surface.
 19.Escape Velocity - can you jump so high that you could fly into space?
20.Gravitational potential energy
21.Center of Gravity and alignment - CoG must be vertically aligned with
 CoB - not only must the push force - normal force on solid and buoyant
 force of liquid be equal, they must also be aligned.
22.Trampoline - normal force is greater than gravitational pull when we apply
 an extra downward push against the trampoline - hence we shoot upwards .
 If we are rest on the trampoline - then its normal force =W, if we give an
 additional push, then it pushes back with N>W+Fextra - which comes from
 the elastic force
23.Gravitas - A person’s quiet authority, presence - from the same root word
 gravis = heavy that gave us gravity,grave, grievance, aggravate - gravity
 pulls on objects physically. gravitas pulls on people emotionally and
 socially.
24.Gravitational waves - ripples in ST due to massive accelerating bodies. This
 wave also propagates at the speed of light

deepest_discoveries_in_physics:
🌌 The Deepest Discoveries in Physics
(Chronological Order)
1. The Idea of Laws of Nature (Ancients → 1600s)

 ● Reality isn’t just divine whim or myth — it follows universal rules.

 ● Seeds in Babylonian astronomy, Greek philosophy, Indian & Chinese cosmologies.

 ● Culminates with Galileo testing motion → nature obeys measurable laws.

2. Newton’s Laws of Motion & Universal Gravitation (1600s)

 ● Unified heaven and Earth: the apple and the Moon follow the same laws.

 ● Introduced the idea that everything is predictable if you know forces + initial conditions.

 ● Birth of classical mechanics.

3. Conservation Laws (1600s–1800s)

 ● Momentum, energy, and angular momentum are conserved.

 ● Invisible bookkeeping of the universe.

 ● Laid groundwork for symmetry principles (later Noether).

4. Wave Nature of Sound & Light (1600s–1800s)

 ● Huygens, Young, Fresnel → interference & diffraction prove light is a wave.
  ● Opened door to thinking of reality as oscillations, not just particles.

5. Thermodynamics & Entropy (1700s–1800s)

 ● Heat is motion of particles, not a substance (“caloric”).

 ● 1st Law: energy is conserved.

 ● 2nd Law: entropy increases → time has a direction.

 ● Deep link between energy, disorder, and the arrow of time.

6. Maxwell’s Unification of Electricity & Magnetism (1860s)

 ● Four equations that show light = electromagnetic wave.

 ● First great unification in physics.

 ● Implies speed of light is universal.

7. Relativity (1905–1915)

 ● Special relativity (Einstein, 1905): time and space are not absolute; E = mc².

 ● General relativity (Einstein, 1915): gravity = curvature of spacetime.

 ● Revolutionized cosmology and astrophysics.

8. Quantum Mechanics (1900–1930s)

 ● Planck, Einstein, Bohr, Schrödinger, Heisenberg, Dirac.
  ● Light and matter = wave–particle duality.

 ● Uncertainty principle: determinism is broken.

 ● Deepest revolution: reality is probabilistic at the core.

9. Nuclear Physics & Quantum Fields (1930s–1950s)

 ● Discovery of nucleus, radioactivity, fission, fusion.

 ● Birth of nuclear power, bombs, and stellar physics.

 ● Quantum electrodynamics (QED): unites quantum mechanics with EM field theory.

10. Standard Model of Particle Physics (1960s–1970s)

 ● All known matter = quarks & leptons.

 ● Forces = exchange of gauge bosons (photon, gluon, W, Z).

 ● Higgs boson gives mass.

 ● The most successful theory we have — but incomplete.

11. Symmetry & Noether’s Theorem (20th Century)

 ● Every conservation law (energy, momentum, charge) arises from a symmetry of nature.

 ● Possibly the deepest principle ever discovered: nature’s bookkeeping is geometry.

12. Cosmic Discoveries (20th Century)
  ● Expansion of the universe (Hubble, 1929).

 ● Cosmic microwave background (1965) → proof of Big Bang.

 ● Dark matter (1930s) & dark energy (1998) → 95% of the universe is “invisible.”

13. Quantum Information & Entanglement (1960s–present)

 ● Bell’s theorem: entanglement is real, no hidden variables.

 ● Quantum computing, quantum teleportation.

 ● Suggests “information” might be more fundamental than matter/energy.

14. Gravitational Waves (2015)

 ● Direct detection of spacetime ripples predicted by Einstein.

 ● Opens a new way of “listening” to the universe.

15. Still Unsolved: The Next Deep Discoveries (Future)

 ● Quantum gravity (uniting relativity + quantum mechanics).

 ● Nature of dark matter & dark energy.

 ● Is information the true “substance” of reality?

 ● Is physics complete, or just scratching the surface?

⚡ Blunt Summary
 The deepest discoveries aren’t just facts — they are shifts in worldview:

 ● The world obeys laws.

 ● The same laws apply everywhere.

 ● Energy is conserved.

 ● Time has an arrow.

 ● Space and time bend.

 ● Reality is probabilistic.

 ● Matter is fields & information.

 ● Most of the universe is still unknown.

Stories of Science

 1. Comic Book Collection

Nikola Tesla

It was a night of storm & lighting in Croatia on July 10, 1856. When the baby boy
drew his first birth. The midwife who delivered him viewed the lighting as a bad
omen & declared him a “child of darkness” to which his mother firmly replied “
He will be a child of light”.

By the 1880s this boy, now a man, Nikola Tesla, was already a certified genius
although with a tinge of crazy , and had won the electricity war against Edison,
with his discovery of the Alternating Current. True to his mother’s words, he was
always playing with current, lighting , light and energy. Many times causing
accidents, burning down his labs and buildings.
It was one such experiment on his quest of wireless energy transfer that burned his
lab in NY this time, that brought him all the way to the mountain top of Colorado,
where he figured, air would be dry & think and hence conduct electricity better.

The town came to life at his arrival - a celebrity. But he hated the attention & did
his best to elude the curious townsfolk and the intrusive reporters, leaving behind
trails of mystery. But news of his various quirks spread wide & fast, about his
strange requests at the hotel he was staying in -from insisting on room number that
is a multiple of 3 -207 ordering 18 fresh towels to his room everyday to his
germaphobic idiosyncrasies.

He got his lab built on the mountain top with a local carpenter - a lab that looked
more like a barn, with a giant Tesla coil & a 142 Feet Pole with a giant copper ball
on top. His experiments began, often shooting out current into the atmosphere -
like Thor’s lighting bolts, lighting up the night sky of the whole town.
 He didn’t stop there. He was also experimenting on conducting electricity through
the Earth to light up bulbs. Because Tesla injected electricity into the ground, the
atmosphere around his laboratory became even more mysterious. Butterflies
flitting around the laboratory seemed disoriented, and passers-by often heard
sparks crackling between their shoes.
He caused several power outages in the area & had to face the wrath of the power
companies that were initially letting him use electricity without cost & had to start
paying for it now. He couldn’t afford it & eventually abandoned the lab and the
town, leaving behind tons of unpaid bills to the power company, water company &
local workers, a trick he would use later towards the end of his life , staying in
hotels, vanishing without making the payments.

genetics_and_gender:
Chromosomes - super packets - contains genes

X chromosomes have ~ 1000s of genes
Y chromosomes now have ~50-70 genes

Metabollic functions, neural development, repair, & many more of the genes specific to
females & the genes required for every organism is retained in the X chromosome.

The Y chromosome packet - has mostly only the genes required for specifically male
functions - hardly 20 genes express outside the purview of testes.

Females have 2 X chromosomes & males 1 X & 1 Y

So females have extra copy of every gene - which makes the XX type more stable &
resilient - if 1 copy of a gene is damaged, it has another copy to fall back on.

Males lack this resilience - If a gene in either of their X or Y chromosome is damaged -
there is no backup.

One of the manifestations of this is the skew of neurodevelopmental disorders in males.

Here begins the biological, neurobiological, behavioural differences in the genders as
determined by genetics.

Y chromosome has the SRY genes - expressed only in males obviously - this gene influences
testes formation - this is the switch that shifts the other default female development of
brain & body to male development. With the SRY gene activated, testosterone surges in
the brain , which is necessary to alter the architecture of the development of the brain to
male setting , instead of the default female plan. Without this, an organism with XY
chromosome’s brain wouldn’t be fully formed.

The other set of influential gene contributing to sexual differences is the Androgen
Receptor genes - this AR gene expression differs by sex, but also by individual. But
largely, statistically, AR gene density is higher in males. AR gene receptors work with the
testosterone - so it is not just how much testosterone there is that determines male
development, brain structures and therefore behaviors, etc - but it is the combination of
both the testosterone level & the AR gene density and the sensitivity of the receptors
which also varies over a range.
This AR gene sits in the X chromosome.
 The SRY gene in the Y chromosome triggers testosterone surge, which activates the AR
gene, proportional to their density & sensitivity across different cells & brain regions.

AR activation is particularly high in brain regions like amygdala, hypothalamus, basal
ganglia, nucleus accumbens - the reward circuit. AR activations in these regions have its
effects -

Amygdala
AR activation:
 ● Increases dendritic growth in threat circuits
 ● Enhances reactivity to dominance challenges
 ● Reduces fear inhibition under competition

Result

 ● Faster aggression response
 ● Greater territorial behavior

Hypothalamus

AR activation:

 ● Expands certain nuclei (e.g., sexually dimorphic nucleus)
 ● Strengthens mating and dominance drives

Result:

 ● Higher drive for rank positioning
 ● Competitive hierarchy sensitivity

Reward circuits (nucleus accumbens / basal ganglia)

AR activation:

 ● Enhances dopamine signaling
 ● Increases reward sensitivity for status, risk & sexual novelty

Result:

 ● Stronger risk loops
 ● Stronger pursuit behaviors
 The next set of genes that contribute to sexual differences is the Estrogen Receptors
present in the X chromosome - which also both males and females have and these
receptors bind with the estradiol - which is also produced in both genders. They modulate
gene transcription to influence development, long term plasticity and also contribute to
fast effects in the synapses, mitochondria, dendritic spines & cell membrane, causing more
short term fluctuations in the body, moods and more- in both genders.

Females show higher baseline ER expression in certain brain regions - hypothalamus, PFC,
hippocampus & amygdala - this expression also fluctuates across the menstrual cycle.
